evidence: AES-256-CBC/PKCS7 decryption returns UTF-8 PowerShell, compiled with ScriptBlock.Create and invoked.

The script repeatedly checks for aspnet_compiler; if absent, Base64/XOR/Base64 unmasks a 64000-byte .NET launcher, loads it with Assembly.Load, and invokes FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER(hostPath, embeddedImage).

Launcher LAUNCHER retries the injection helper up to five times. Its initializer orders twelve delegates: create suspended hidden process (0x08000004), parse PE, get x86/WOW64 thread context, read PEB image base, conditionally unmap image, allocate RWX remote image, write headers and sections, replace PEB image base, set CONTEXT[44] to allocation plus entry RVA, set context, resume thread. Failure kills the created process.

CIL methods 0x06-0x11 prove remote image replacement and execution transfer. The embedded native image is 284160 bytes, importless and high entropy. The outer script sleeps five seconds and retries when its host disappears.
Four hostile detections cover encrypted script evaluation, masked assembly activation and native-host transplantation. All retained; no missing payload-family behavior was inferred.
samples.limitations: Final packed native payload family and runtime success are unestablished. No network beacon is established by the loop name.

evidence: All six wheel members were inspected. The .pth imports _boot, whose module-level bootstrap collects a snapshot on each interpreter startup. __init__.runs reads the two snapshot directories.
Snapshot includes up to 200 process records with argv, all environment values truncated to 200 characters, cwd, uid/gid, runtime paths, boot identifiers, hostname, DNS/TCP probes and HTTP responses.

HTTP requests read the GCP recursive metadata listing, default service-account email, and PyPI index. Socket probes connect and close. No explicit metadata token path is requested. Environment and metadata may nevertheless contain sensitive data.

bootstrap serializes to JSON and writes under the package _runs directory and /tmp/package-name. No snapshot data reaches any network request: request URLs and headers are fixed and there is no upload, command dispatch, concealed payload or code execution beyond the disclosed startup hook.

METADATA accurately discloses startup activation, process/environment collection, metadata listing and both local destinations. This alignment, reviewable source and absence of a demonstrated unauthorized collection context tip the judgment toward benign diagnostics. Three suspicious reconnaissance/startup findings are accurate and retained.
